### 📦 Phase 26: Unified Dual-Role Accounts & Explicit Role-Switching
> Resolves the identity collision where `Account.email @unique` blocks an artist from booking as a client under the same email profile.
- [ ] **26.1: Dual-Role Core Engine Setup**
  - **Prerequisite Architecture pass:** Enforce the design constraint that an artist's linked client identity must use a standard `ClientProfile` row so precharge models apply naturally.
  - **Architecture decision (confirmed):** `Account.role` stays the account's permanent home role; a new `Session.activeRole` column holds the per-session effective role (dual-role accounts may hold concurrent sessions in different roles; `activeRole` must stay server-trusted for `src/proxy.ts` gating, so it lives in the DB, not a client-readable cookie). Becoming dual-role is an explicit "Become a client" settings action (never automatic, never auto-switches into the new role afterward). Shared Instagram-handle/18+ validation primitives move to `src/lib/clientProfileValidation.ts`; the `ClientProfile` find-or-link matching logic stays auth-owned (not shared with booking's guest-checkout `resolveGuestClientProfile`, whose overwrite-on-repeat-visit semantics are wrong for a one-time authenticated link).
  - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):

    - [x] **26.1.2.2** Domain Service — `createSession` accepts `activeRole` (required; caller passes the account's role — landed as required, not optional/defaulted, in PR #202).

### 📦 Phase 27: Auth Session Security & Lifecycle Hardening ◄ CURRENT FOCUS
- **Status:** 27.1–27.2 scoped; 27.3–27.5 remain unscoped (each will get its own layered breakdown pass closer to when it's picked up).
- **Objectives:** Gaps surfaced during review of the Phase 26 dual-role/session work, ordered by priority for production risk:
  - **27.1: Login throttling/lockout** — `loginArtist`/`loginClient` do scrypt-verify with no rate limit or attempt counter; no backstop against credential stuffing beyond hash cost. Highest priority: active, unmitigated attack surface.
    - **Design (confirmed):** account-scoped lockout (no IP-based tracking — no request-IP capture infra exists in the repo, out of scope here). Two new `Account` fields: `failedLoginAttempts Int @default(0)` and `lockedUntil DateTime?`. A locked account returns the *same* generic `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR_MESSAGE` (never a distinct "account locked" message) so lockout state doesn't become a new enumeration vector on top of the existing generic-error protection — `verifyPassword` is skipped entirely while locked. A failed attempt after a naturally-expired lockout window restarts the counter at 1 rather than instantly re-locking. Successful login resets both fields. Constants `MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5` / `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_DURATION_MS = 15 min` land in `src/domains/auth/constants.ts`. Accepted tradeoff: skipping `verifyPassword` while locked is a minor timing side-channel (locked responses return faster than wrong-password ones); not hardened further given the app's risk profile. No UI/Hook/View changes needed — `useArtistLogin`/`useClientLogin` already forward any `result.error` string generically into the existing login forms' error state, and the lockout path reuses the existing message, so the presentation layer is untouched.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [ ] **27.1.1.1** Data Gateway — add `Account.failedLoginAttempts Int @default(0)` + `Account.lockedUntil DateTime?` columns + migration. No app code.
      - [ ] **27.1.2.1** Domain Service — `recordFailedLoginAttempt(account)` in `services/recordFailedLoginAttempt.ts` (mocked-Prisma unit tests: first failure, Nth failure hits `MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS`, failure after a naturally-expired lockout restarts the counter at 1).
      - [ ] **27.1.2.2** Domain Service — `resetFailedLoginAttempts(accountId)` in `services/resetFailedLoginAttempts.ts` (mocked-Prisma unit test).
      - [ ] **27.1.2.3** Domain Service — wire the lockout check + `recordFailedLoginAttempt`/`resetFailedLoginAttempts` into `loginArtist.ts` and `loginClient.ts`; extend their existing `.test.ts` files (locked account short-circuits before `verifyPassword`, failed attempt records, success resets).
      - [ ] **27.1.3.1** Controller/Action — N/A. `loginAction`/`loginClientAction` already pass `result.error` through unchanged; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.
      - [ ] **27.1.4.1** UI Primitive — N/A. Existing `LoginForm`/`ClientLoginForm` error rendering already covers this.
      - [ ] **27.1.5.1** Domain Hook — N/A. `useArtistLogin`/`useClientLogin` already forward `result.error` generically.
      - [ ] **27.1.6.1** View & Route — N/A. No new routes or page composition required.
  - **27.2: Defensive error isolation on internal DB paths** — `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` uses `findUniqueOrThrow` inside a transaction; the calling action (`setUpClientProfileAction`, the actual name in code — the roadmap's `becomeClientAction` label in Phase 26 doesn't match `actions.ts`, worth reconciling when Phase 26 closes) doesn't catch it, so an edge-case failure bubbles as an uncaught 500. Apply the same try/catch isolation discipline architecture.md §6 requires for Stripe calls to this internal DB path.
    - **Design (confirmed):** wrap the entire `prisma.$transaction(...)` call in `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts` in one try/catch (sufficient by Prisma semantics — any throw inside the callback surfaces at the outer call, so no nested try/catch is needed; the transaction's existing `{success:false,...}` business-error returns are untouched). Deeper analysis surfaced two things beyond a bare wrapper: (1) `ClientProfile.instagramHandle`/`email` are both `@unique` with no explicit transaction isolation level set (default Postgres Read Committed), so the check-then-`create` flow has a genuine TOCTOU race — two concurrent submits can both pass the "no match" check and collide on `tx.clientProfile.create` with Prisma error P2002; (2) `useSetUpClientProfile.ts`'s `onSubmit` has no try/catch around `await setUpClientProfileAction(...)`, so an uncaught throw today leaves the form in a stuck-spinner state, not just a generic 500 — the concrete reason this must be fixed at the service boundary rather than left to the hook. Unlike the sibling precedent in `booking/services/updateClientProfile.ts` (which maps its own P2002 to one unambiguous message and rethrows everything else), this service must never rethrow (that's exactly the stuck-spinner bug) and must not map P2002 to a specific "already linked" message (ambiguous here — could mean self double-submit *or* a genuine two-user race, and guessing wrong is actively misleading). Both the P2002 case and any other unexpected error return the same new generic, retry-oriented `SET_UP_CLIENT_PROFILE_UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE`; a retry self-corrects via the service's existing lookup logic either way. P2002 is still distinguished from other errors in the `console.error` log line only (accountId, never PII), for ops triage. `findUniqueOrThrow`'s P2025 is structurally near-unreachable (`Session.account` has `onDelete: Cascade`, so a live session can't reference a deleted account) but still caught defensively — no session-invalidation logic is built around it, since no reachable state requires it.
    - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (single isolated PR — no other layer has any change):
      - [ ] **27.2.1.1** Data Gateway — N/A, no schema change.
      - [ ] **27.2.2.1** Domain Service — try/catch wrapper + `isClientProfileUniqueConflict` P2002 helper (mirrors `updateClientProfile.ts`'s `isInstagramHandleConflict`) + `SET_UP_CLIENT_PROFILE_UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE` constant in `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts`; extend `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.test.ts` with: generic-Error rejection → generic result not thrown; P2002 rejection → same generic result (proving the P2002 split is log-only); a `console.error` spy asserting both cases log.
      - [ ] **27.2.3.1–27.2.6.1** Controller/UI/Hook/View — N/A. Fixing the service boundary neutralizes `useSetUpClientProfile.ts`'s stuck-spinner gap by construction; the hook itself is untouched.
  - **27.3: Email verification before session issuance** — `signupClient` grants a session immediately on account creation with no proof of email ownership. There is no `signupArtist` (artist accounts are manually provisioned per CLAUDE.md 5.1), so this is the only account-creation-time session issuance in the codebase.
    - **Design (confirmed):** Provider is Resend (new dependency + `src/lib/resend.ts` singleton wrapper mirroring `src/lib/stripe.ts`); no backfill needed (no real users to grandfather as verified). Verification UX is a 6-digit numeric code (not a magic link — resilient to email-client link prefetching) entered on a dedicated `/client/verify-email` page. Session-issuance model is "no session until verified": `signupClient` creates the `Account`, generates+stores a hashed code, sends the email, and returns a pending-verification result with no session fields — it no longer calls `createSession`. `verifyEmailCode` is the only path that issues the session for a fresh signup (auto-login on correct code, no separate password re-entry). `loginClient` gets defense-in-depth: since password ownership is already proven before this check, an unverified account with a correct password returns a distinct `pendingVerification` result (no session) rather than succeeding — this is not a new enumeration vector, unlike a pre-auth check would be. `resendVerificationCode` always returns the same generic result regardless of account existence/verified state/cooldown, for the same enumeration-safety reason `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR_MESSAGE` is generic. Brute-force protection: `MAX_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPTS = 5` wrong guesses invalidates the current code (forces a resend) since a 6-digit keyspace isn't safe against unlimited guessing; `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_CODE_EXPIRY_MS = 15 min`; `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS = 60s` to throttle resend-spam/cost. Code storage is sha256 (`node:crypto createHash`, compared with `timingSafeEqual`) rather than scrypt — the code is short-lived and rate-limited, unlike a password, so scrypt's deliberate slowness has no benefit and would slow the verify path for nothing. The Resend call itself follows architecture.md §6 exactly (isolated try/catch, never rethrow, generic error on failure), mirroring `createConnectOnboardingLink.ts`. Playwright can't receive real emails, so `sendVerificationEmail` gets a test-only branch (env-flag gated, never set in production) that writes `{email, code}` to a capture sink instead of calling Resend; e2e reads the real code back through that sink, exercising the hashing/storage/verification logic unmodified. Implementation reminders: Prisma Update Atomicity in `verifyEmailCode`, Cooldown Logic in `resendVerificationCode` and Client-Side Form Usability in `VerifyEmailCodeForm`.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [ ] **27.3.1.1** Data Gateway — add `Account.emailVerifiedAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeHash String?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeExpiresAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeSentAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationAttempts Int @default(0)` + migration. No app code, no backfill.
      - [ ] **27.3.2.1** Domain Service — add `resend` npm dependency; `src/lib/resend.ts` singleton wrapper; add `RESEND_API_KEY`/`EMAIL_FROM` dummy env values to the `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
      - [ ] **27.3.2.2** Domain Service — `services/generateEmailVerificationCode.ts` (pure helper: `crypto.randomInt` 6-digit code, sha256 hash, expiry timestamp; unit test).
      - [ ] **27.3.2.3** Domain Service — `services/sendVerificationEmail.ts` (try/catch-wrapped `resend.emails.send`, per architecture.md §6; test-mode capture-sink branch for e2e; unit test with mocked `@/lib/resend`).
      - [ ] **27.3.2.4** Domain Service — modify `signupClient.ts`: generate+persist code, call `sendVerificationEmail`, remove `createSession`, return the new pending-verification result shape; extend `signupClient.test.ts`.
      - [ ] **27.3.2.5** Domain Service — `services/verifyEmailCode.ts` (hash/expiry/attempt-count validation, `timingSafeEqual`, code invalidation after max attempts, `createSession` on success; unit tests: correct/wrong/expired/max-attempts/already-verified/unknown-email).
      - [ ] **27.3.2.6** Domain Service — `services/resendVerificationCode.ts` (cooldown-gated regenerate+resend, generic result regardless of account state; unit test).
      - [ ] **27.3.2.7** Domain Service — modify `loginClient.ts`: unverified account + correct password short-circuits into `pendingVerification` (no session); extend `loginClient.test.ts`.
      - [ ] **27.3.3.1** Controller/Action — `verifyEmailCodeInputSchema`/`resendVerificationCodeInputSchema` in `auth.schema.ts`; `verifyEmailCodeAction`/`resendVerificationCodeAction` in `actions.ts` (sets session cookie via existing `setSessionCookie` helper on successful verification).
      - [ ] **27.3.3.2** Controller/Action — update `signupClientAction`/`loginClientAction` result types/branches to carry the pending-verification outcome through.
      - [ ] **27.3.4.1** UI Primitive — `VerifyEmailCodeForm` component (6-digit input, resend button with cooldown countdown, error state; mirrors `ClientLoginForm`/`ClientSignupForm`, semantic tokens only).
      - [ ] **27.3.5.1** Domain Hook — `useVerifyEmailCode.ts` (form state + resend cooldown timer + redirect to `/client` on success; hook test via `renderHook`, mirrors `useSwitchActiveRole.test.ts`).
      - [ ] **27.3.5.2** Domain Hook — modify `useClientSignup.ts`/`useClientLogin.ts` to redirect to `/client/verify-email?email=...` on the pending-verification outcome; update/extend their hook tests.
      - [ ] **27.3.6.1** View & Route — new `/client/verify-email` page; add its path to `PUBLIC_CLIENT_PATHS` in `src/proxy.ts`; `e2e/verify-email.spec.ts` with a `toHaveScreenshot()` assertion using the capture-sink bypass; update the existing client-signup e2e spec to route through verification.
  - **27.4: Session TTL/cleanup** — session rows are created on every login/signup and never pruned; `switchActiveRole`/`getSessionWithAccount` only filter expired rows at read time — no sweep/cron job exists. Growth/scale risk, not an active exploit: an ever-growing, unindexed `Session` table directly degrades the hot path of every authenticated request (`src/proxy.ts` hits Postgres on every matched request), not just an offline job's runtime.
    - **Design (confirmed):** No cron/scheduler infra exists anywhere in the repo today (no `vercel.json`, no `/api/cron` routes, no scheduled GitHub Actions, no cron/queue dependency), and the hosting platform is never confirmed in-repo. Trigger mechanism (user-confirmed): a new `.github/workflows/session-cleanup.yml` scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (daily `schedule:` cron `0 3 * * *` + `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs) — platform-agnostic rather than assuming Vercel Cron, and this repo already uses GitHub Actions for CI. The workflow does an authenticated `curl POST` (using `CRON_SECRET`/`APP_URL` repo secrets) to a new `src/app/api/cron/session-cleanup/route.ts` route, which mirrors the existing `src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts` pattern (closest existing precedent for an externally-triggered, secret-verified endpoint). The route validates `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` via a length-safe `crypto.timingSafeEqual` compare (reject immediately on length mismatch before comparing, never throw; no DB touch at all on a bad/missing secret — mirrors the constant-time discipline already established for email verification codes in 27.3), returning `401` on failure. On a valid secret it delegates to the domain service inside a try/catch (architecture.md §6 discipline), returning generic `500` + server-side log (no PII) on failure or `200` with `{ deletedCount, durationMs }` on success for ops visibility in the Action's job log. Prisma's `deleteMany` has no `LIMIT`, so a single invocation against a large table risks a long-running transaction/lock; the domain service instead loops a raw-SQL batched delete (`DELETE FROM "Session" WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "Session" WHERE "expiresAt" < now() LIMIT $1)` via `prisma.$executeRaw`), stopping when a batch returns 0 rows or a max-batch cap is hit, so one invocation's runtime is bounded regardless of backlog size. New constants `SESSION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE = 1000` / `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES = 20` (bounds one run to 20,000 deletions; a larger backlog just finishes on the next day's run). Concurrency safety is deliberate-no-locking: a raw `DELETE ... WHERE expiresAt < now()` is naturally idempotent, so an overlapping manual + scheduled run just has the later one delete 0 rows for already-removed ids — no read-then-write race exists. `Session.expiresAt` has no index today, so a `@@index([expiresAt])` migration is required or the batched delete's inner `SELECT` is a full table scan. `CRON_SECRET` is added to `.env.example` and the CI `test` job's dummy-env block (same non-secret-placeholder pattern as `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`UPLOADTHING_TOKEN`, and already planned for `RESEND_API_KEY` in 27.3.2.1) purely so the route module doesn't crash import-time env checks in CI — the workflow itself only ever runs against a real deployed `APP_URL`, never inside `ci.yml`'s Postgres-container job. Explicitly deferred, not bundled in: `getSessionWithAccount.ts` and `switchActiveRole.ts` independently hand-roll the same `expiresAt.getTime() <= Date.now()` check — a legitimate architecture.md §5 "Shared Logic Extraction" candidate, but orthogonal to pruning rows and out of this atomic scope.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [ ] **27.4.1.1** Data Gateway — add `@@index([expiresAt])` to the `Session` model + migration. No app code.
      - [ ] **27.4.2.1** Domain Service — add `SESSION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE` / `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES` constants to `src/domains/auth/constants.ts`.
      - [ ] **27.4.2.2** Domain Service — `services/pruneExpiredSessions.ts` (batched raw-SQL delete loop via `prisma.$executeRaw`, returns total deleted count; mocked-Prisma unit tests mirroring `switchActiveRole.test.ts`'s style: single partial batch, multi-batch loop terminating on a zero-row batch, loop terminating at `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES`, and a zero-expired-rows no-op).
      - [ ] **27.4.3.1** Controller/Action — `src/app/api/cron/session-cleanup/route.ts` `POST` handler (length-safe `timingSafeEqual` bearer-token check against `CRON_SECRET`, delegates to `pruneExpiredSessions`, try/catch → generic `500` + server-side log, `200` with `{ deletedCount, durationMs }` on success); add `CRON_SECRET` to `.env.example` and the CI dummy-env block; route-handler unit test invoking the exported `POST` directly with mocked service (missing secret → 401, mismatched secret → 401, success → 200 with mocked count, service throws → 500).
      - [ ] **27.4.4.1** UI Primitive — N/A. No user-facing surface exists for a backend sweep job; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.
      - [ ] **27.4.5.1** Domain Hook — N/A. No client-side state to orchestrate.
      - [ ] **27.4.6.1** View & Route — new `.github/workflows/session-cleanup.yml` (`schedule:` daily cron + `workflow_dispatch`, authenticated `curl POST` to the route using the `CRON_SECRET`/`APP_URL` repo secrets). This is the layer that actually wires the endpoint into a live, recurring invocation path — the closest analog this backend-only feature has to "View & Route."
  - **27.5: Audit trail on security-relevant events** — role switches, failed logins, and Set Up Client Profile links aren't logged anywhere; given CLAUDE.md's cancellation/precharge flagging requirements on `ClientProfile`, an audit trail on identity/role changes belongs at this level. Lowest urgency of the five: compliance/forensics value, not a live gap.
    - **Design (confirmed):** new append-only `AuditEvent` Prisma model — `eventType`/`outcome`/`reasonCode` are all DB-enforced enums (`AuditEventType`, `AuditEventOutcome`, `AuditReasonCode`), never free-form strings, so no typo'd value can ever land in the table. `accountId` is nullable with `onDelete: SetNull` (unlike `Session`'s `Cascade`) — an audit row must outlive account deletion for forensic value. `attemptedEmail` is populated only when there's no `accountId` to attach to (account-not-found/role-mismatch login failures), to detect enumeration/credential-stuffing scanning; this never leaves the server (the caller still gets the same generic error), so it's an accepted data-minimization tradeoff, same posture as 27.1's accepted timing side-channel. No IP-address field — no request-IP infra exists in the repo (same finding as 27.1). Indexed on `(accountId, createdAt)` and `(eventType, createdAt)` for compliance queries. Scoped to today's actual code, not 27.1–27.4's still-unimplemented designs, since phases have no guaranteed merge order. Single write choke point: `services/recordAuditEvent.ts` wraps `prisma.auditEvent.create` in its own try/catch (architecture.md §6 discipline) — never throws, always resolves `void`, logs `console.error` with only `eventType`/`reasonCode`/`accountId` on failure (never `attemptedEmail`), mirroring the ID-only logging convention in `billing/services/createArtistConnectAccount.ts`/`refundDeposit.ts`. Every call site awaits it (so a serverless function doesn't terminate before the write lands) but its result never affects the caller's return value or control flow. Call sites: `loginArtist.ts`/`loginClient.ts` audit **failures only** (`ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`/`ROLE_MISMATCH` with `attemptedEmail`, `INVALID_PASSWORD` with `accountId`) — successful logins aren't in scope. `switchActiveRole.ts` audits both "not linked to X" rejections and the success path (all with `accountId`+`targetRole`); the session-not-found/expired branch is skipped (no reliable identity to attach). `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts` (the Set Up Client Profile flow) calls `recordAuditEvent` once, after `prisma.$transaction(...)` resolves (decoupled from transaction rollback semantics), branching on the already-discriminated result — both rejection reasons and both success reasons (profile created vs. matched-existing), always with `accountId`. No presentation layer: no admin UI, query surface, retention/export policy, or IP capture — mirrors 27.4.4.1's precedent of explicitly reserving UI/Hook/View/Controller leaves as N/A for a backend-only, compliance-facing feature. Explicitly deferred: an audit-log viewer, retention/archival policy, and auditing additional event types (successful logins, logout, 27.1's lockout triggers, 27.3's email-verification events) — bundling those here would violate the atomic-scope rule.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [ ] **27.5.1.1** Data Gateway — add `AuditEvent` model, `AuditEventType`/`AuditEventOutcome`/`AuditReasonCode` enums, and `Account.auditEvents` back-relation + migration. No app code.
      - [ ] **27.5.2.1** Domain Service — `services/recordAuditEvent.ts` (try/catch wrapper around `prisma.auditEvent.create`, never throws, console.error on failure logs only `eventType`/`reasonCode`/`accountId`; mocked-Prisma unit tests: successful create, create-throws is swallowed + console.error spy assertion never includes `attemptedEmail`).
      - [ ] **27.5.2.2** Domain Service — wire `recordAuditEvent` into `loginArtist.ts` and `loginClient.ts` failure branches only; extend their `.test.ts` files (mock `recordAuditEvent`, assert `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`/`ROLE_MISMATCH` branch calls with `attemptedEmail` + no `accountId`, `INVALID_PASSWORD` branch calls with `accountId` + no `attemptedEmail`, success path does not call it).
      - [ ] **27.5.2.3** Domain Service — wire `recordAuditEvent` into `switchActiveRole.ts` (both "not linked" rejection branches + the success branch; session-not-found branch intentionally skipped); extend `switchActiveRole.test.ts`.
      - [ ] **27.5.2.4** Domain Service — wire `recordAuditEvent` into `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts`, called once after the transaction resolves, branching on the discriminated result; extend `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.test.ts`.
      - [ ] **27.5.3.1** Controller/Action — N/A. Audit writes live entirely in the service layer; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.
      - [ ] **27.5.4.1** UI Primitive — N/A. No user-facing surface for a compliance/forensics log (mirrors 27.4.4.1's precedent).
      - [ ] **27.5.5.1** Domain Hook — N/A.
      - [ ] **27.5.6.1** View & Route — N/A. No admin/audit-viewing UI in scope (explicitly deferred, see Design above).
  - **Callout:** once Phase 26's remaining item (`26.1.6.2`) lands, verify the existing "Become a client" + `RoleSwitcher` dual-role design already covers an artist booking as a client with another artist — this was a note from refinement, not a confirmed gap.

### 📦 Phase 28: Domain Testing Architecture & Test Layer Migration
- **Status:** Unscoped.
- **Objectives:** Migrate all existing domain tests to use a lightweight, mocked Prisma layer for fast unit testing, while establishing a dedicated real-database integration and E2E testing framework to validate complex multi-domain database constraints and transaction boundary guarantees. Extended scope, priority-ordered: (1) controller/action-layer (`actions.ts`) test coverage — the thin action layer doing session-check + validation + redirect branching is currently untested despite testing.md's edge-case mandate, and it directly wraps the security-sensitive paths in Phase 27 above; (2) hook-level unit tests using `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` for every domain hook (none currently exist, despite every service having a `.test.ts`).
